transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ruiz (CTO, Northshore AI), Amit Singh (ML Eng), Sofia Park (VP Product)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. we're, uh, Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. today Liam from our solutions engineering team's gonna walk through model trade-offs and technical questions. quick round robin?
[00:15] Elena: Hi, Elena here. quick background — we're building an AI assistant for customer support and developer docs, target multilingual coverage (english, spanish, french), and we need pretty long context windows, at least 8k tokens but optimizing toward 32k for multi-doc reasoning.
[00:35] Amit: Amit, ML eng, i'll own the benchmark side and provide sample prompts.
[00:40] Sofia: Sofia, product — focused on latency targets and cost.
[00:45] Liam: Great. quick agenda: model selection (open models), context/quantization tradeoffs, tool calling/function support, and deployment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) for compliance.

[02:10] Maya: can you talk briefly about what you currently run? infra, vectors, any existing models?
[02:20] Elena: currently we run a mixed setup — embeddings on a hosted vector db (managed), some smaller models on prem for redaction, and we trialled a couple of hosted LLM APIs. main pain is unpredictability in latency and cost when traffic spikes, and we also have PII concerns for certain flows.
[02:45] Maya: got it. that maps to the typical Hosted vs Dedicated conversation — hosted gives fastest time-to-value, but Dedicated or Private gives you isolation and predictable throughput.

[05:00] Liam: on model selection — you said multilingual and long context. for open models, candidates are Llama2/3 variants, Mistral-based models, and some community 8k/32k variants. goal is: accuracy on English + Spanish + French, and deterministic tool-calling for retrieval.
[05:25] Amit: we're sensitive to hallucinations for retrieval tasks; need function-calling that returns structured JSON so our app can reliably parse.
[05:40] Liam: Redwood supports function/tool-calling patterns — we can stream structured outputs and we support deterministic function hooks. small caveat, some community models need prompt engineering to be reliable on strict JSON, but our rollout tooling and output validation can help.

[07:30] Elena: curious about context length implications. is 32k practical in Dedicated? what about token pricing?
[07:45] Liam: 32k is practical but impacts memory and throughput. on Dedicated pools you can size GPUs to handle long context — and Redwood picks kernels and quantization that are best fit. cost goes up roughly linearly with sequence length for generation-heavy workloads, but batching and KV cache reduce repeated prefix costs.
[08:30] Maya: also we provide model variants and fallbacks — e.g. smaller quantized variants for less critical flows to save cost, and higher-quality variants for core QA.

[10:00] Sofia: For latency, our SLO is sub 400ms for short-turn queries and under 2s for longer context generation. is that reasonable?
[10:15] Liam: For hosted low-latency at scale it's challenging; Dedicated with reserved capacity is more predictable. sub-400ms depends on prompt size, model size, and batch windows. we can tune batch windows and CPU-to-GPU ratios. quantized 8-bit models often give good latency but we need to verify quality.

[12:20] Elena: security — SOC2 is a must. we also use customer-managed KMS, SOC2 + ISO would be ideal. anything else?
[12:35] Maya: we have SOC2 reports, and for Private/on-prem we support customer KMS or HSM integrations. also VPC peering and SAML SSO + RBAC. we can share the security whitepaper after this call.

[14:50] Amit: about embeddings and retrieval: we currently use namespace separation per customer and want audit logs for vector access.
[15:05] Liam: Redwood Console provides per-route and token-level tracing and audit logs. for Private setups we can forward logs to your SIEM and keep retention policies per customer.

[17:40] Elena: model accuracy — do you benchmark across languages?
[17:50] Liam: yes, SE-led benchmarks typically run per-language prompt sets. we recommend client-supplied prompts for best signal. we can run across Llama 2-70B+, Mistral x-weights, and community 32k context forks. note: some models labeled 32k are actually sliding-window approaches and need careful kernel support — Redwood's runtime includes optimized KV cache and seq-parallel kernels that help.

[20:10] Sofia: what's the overhead of quantization on hallucination rates?
[20:20] Liam: quantization (8-bit, 4-bit) can slightly change generation behavior. we usually do a quality regression suite tied to eval prompts; Redwood Optimize suggests quant profiles per workload. for critical flows we recommend A/B with fallback if quality drops.

[22:45] Amit: tool-calling detail — can Redwood handle external DB calls within the model flow? like call to search+return structured fields?
[22:55] Liam: yes, function-calling is supported. we also provide a tool layer for safe sandboxing. for low-latency retrieval we recommend local vector stores colocated with Dedicated pools or using prefix caching.

[25:10] Elena: our compliance team also wants data residency — store vectors in EU region for EU customers.
[25:20] Maya: doable — region routing policies and per-customer routing is supported. Private deployments can be in your VPC or on-prem for strictest requirements.

[27:00] Sofia: pricing question: how different is Dedicated vs Hosted cost model?
[27:10] Maya: Hosted is usage-based, per-token + per-embed. Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits — higher base but predictable unit costs and better latency guarantees. Private is license + infra. we'll send a tailored estimate.

[29:30] Liam: technical deep-dive we propose: run your provided prompts against Llama 2-70B quantized, Mistral-XX-32k candidate, and a higher-memory LLM to compare hallucination and latency on 8k/32k.
[29:50] Amit: yes please. we'll provide a 2k sample prompt set and some retrieval contexts.

[31:00] Elena: any gotchas with KV cache? we do a lot of multi-turn chat where tokens accumulate.
[31:10] Liam: KV cache reduces recomputation for repeated prefixes. for multi-turn you want a runtime that preserves K-V efficiently and supports eviction policies; Redwood's runtime manages K-V cache and supports partial prefix caching. small transcription note: sometimes docs call it K-V cash, lol.

[33:40] Maya: do you have preferred open models? we can recommend based on your latency vs accuracy needs.
[33:50] Liam: quick shorthand: if you need best quality + large context => Llama-3 style or Mistral with 32k variants; if cost-sensitive, a tuned 8-bit quantized Llama2-70B or Mistral medium variant is a good trade. also consider retrieval-augmented pipelines to reduce generation tokens.

[36:10] Sofia: how does Redwood handle rollouts and regressions? we can't risk a change that increases hallucination.
[36:20] Maya: Console supports rollouts, canary, A/B, and automatic fallback. Redwood Optimize ties evals to prompt sets and will alert on regressions.

[38:00] Elena: on private/on-prem — latency is better but ops overhead is higher, right?
[38:10] Liam: yes, Private gives you control but you manage infra. Redwood provides the control plane and deployment artifacts; we have an appliance for air-gapped environments. Dedicated is middle ground — dedicated GPU pools managed by Redwood in your cloud region.

[41:30] Amit: competitor question — some teams like Anthropic for instruction finetuning. any differences we should be aware of?
[41:40] Liam: Anthropic and OpenAI have managed models and unique safety frameworks. open models give you more control (weights, quant, on-prem). Redwood supports both hosting and private weights onboarding for vetted open models.

[43:00] Sofia: any recommended immediate experiment?
[43:10] Liam: start with a Hosted proof-of-concept using an 8k quantized Llama2-70B-ish variant to validate prompt flows and function-calling. run parallel Dedicated benchmark for 8k/32k to compare latency/cost.

[45:05] Elena: recap for internal notes: we need pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated; security pack; SE benchmark run with our prompts; and clarify region/residency and KMS options.
[45:30] Maya: perfect. i'll follow up with pricing and SOC2 doc today. Liam will kick off the benchmark setup and we should aim to reconvene after initial bench results.
[45:45] Amit: we'll send data and prompts by Monday.
[46:00] Sofia: thanks everyone.
[46:10] Maya: thanks all, end call.
